title: Ephemeral Data Strategy — FinServ POC (Draft)
content:
Context:
This is a working draft for the FinServ pilot request: customer requires a POC demonstrating that Redwood can host inference for sensitive banking workflows while minimizing retention of customer-provided conversational data. They asked for two guarantees: 1) no persistent storage of raw prompts/outputs beyond a strictly bounded window, and 2) an auditable path to prove deletion/ephemerality for audit and contractual purposes (DPA addendum).

High-level proposal summary:
- Introduce an "ephemeralization" operating mode for the POC: runtime-only KV cache, no disk-backed session logs, telemetry hashed & sampled, and a narrow retention bucket for billing/metrics only.
- Provide an addendum template with 3 retention tiers the customer can choose from: Session-only (default), Short-term trace (7 days, hashed), Minimal billing records (30 days, tokens-only, aggregated).
- Integrate customer-managed KMS for key separation so audit logs can be independently verified (customer retains key).

Goals for the POC:
1) Demonstrate a reproducible deployment that processes live test conversations but never writes raw messages to durable storage after the session closes.
2) Produce an audit report with evidence of deletion procedures and cryptographic proofs (KMS-wrapped deletion markers).
3) Show fallback behaviors: if Dedicated capacity is unavailable, requests fall back to a limited hosted variant that still respects ephemeral settings.

Design details (technical):
1) Runtime mode: Ephemeral Session
   - Inference nodes run with a transient-only memstore for KV cache. No /var/log or application-level persistent storage of message-level inputs/outputs when ephemeral mode is enabled.
   - Session lifecycle: session_start -> ephemeral cache active -> session_end triggers immediate in-memory purge and a KMS-wrapped deletion event posted to the control plane.

2) Telemetry & observability
   - Metrics: counts/latency/aggregate token consumption are emitted as numeric aggregates (no raw text).
   - Traces: request IDs and timing are recorded; payloads never persisted to long-term tracing backends unless explicitly flagged by customer.
   - Debugging flow: if debug mode toggled by SE/CS, a short-lived debug container can be spun which stores encrypted transcripts into a customer-owned S3 bucket for up to 72 hours (explicit customer opt-in).

3) Minimal persistent retention for billing
   - For billing reconciliation we keep a per-request numeric record: model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp, route_id. No prompt/response text. TTL default 30 days, configurable down to 0 (no retention).

4) Hashing and pseudonymization
   - For customers who require limited retention for model quality, we propose salted HMAC(SHA256) of prompts using a customer-provided salt (rotated monthly) so exact text cannot be reconstructed from stored records.

5) Redaction pipeline (optional)
   - Client-side SDK helper: best-effort PII scrub and pattern redaction (SSNs, account numbers). Not a substitute for customer-side data minimization — we provide examples and regex sets.

6) Key management
   - Customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM) for encrypting any persisted debug transcripts and for signing deletion receipts. Redwood holds no access to the plaintext when customer keys are used.

Operational proofs & auditables:
- Deletion receipts: signed token that includes session_id, deletion_timestamp, hashed session summary, and KMS-sig. Stored for up to 7 years depending on contract (note: receipts do not include raw content).
- Tamper-evident audit trails: append-only ledger of deletion events with cryptographic chain (Merkle-ish), retained in customer-visible S3 with read-only policies.
- Test harness: we will run 20 scripted sessions and show logs: session creation, active inference, session end, in-memory purge, receipt generation, and receipt verification steps.

DPA addendum draft snippets (language for Legal to review):
- Data scope: "Customer Data" means inputs and prompts submitted by Customer end-users. Redwood will process Customer Data solely for the purposes of inference and transiently store such data only in-memory during active sessions.
- Ephemerality obligation: "Redwood shall not persist Customer Data in durable storage beyond the configured session TTL. Upon session termination, Redwood will purge in-memory caches and emit a cryptographically-signed deletion receipt to Customer."
- KMS/Encryption: "Customer may configure a customer-managed key (CMK) to encrypt any persisted artifacts used for debugging or billing; Redwood will not retain the CMK or plaintext when CMK is configured."
- Audit rights: "On a quarterly basis or under reasonable notice, Redwood will provide Customer with signed deletion receipts and supporting metadata for sessions covered by this POC."
- Exceptions: "Redwood may retain aggregated telemetry necessary for billing and platform health. Aggregated metrics will not include raw textual content and will not be used to reconstruct Customer Data."

Deployment checklist (engineers + SE):
- [ ] Confirm customer's KMS provider and create CMK access role (Jira: SE-7842).
- [ ] Prepare ephemeral runtime AMI/container image with disk writes disabled and memstore-only configuration.
- [ ] Create S3 bucket with customer-managed encryption for deletion receipts and ledger.
- [ ] Implement toggle in config: EPHEMERAL_MODE=true; ensure flags propagate to autoscaling groups.
- [ ] Run 20 scripted verification sessions and collect receipts.
- [ ] Legal: finalize DPA addendum (Legal-3210).
- [ ] Run a failure mode test where a node crashes mid-session and validate that no partial transcripts are recoverable.

Operational runbook (short):
- On deployment day: enable EPHEMERAL_MODE in canary pool, run smoke tests, review receipts.
- Incident: if customer requests retention rollback, only Product + Legal can approve; all changes are logged and require signed authorization.

Open questions / risks (notes to self and for legal/infra):
- Q: Are deletion receipts acceptable as evidence in regulated audits? Legal needs to review (Clara).
- Q: Will customers accept hashed prompts for quality monitoring? Some fintech ops will need a redaction + limited-review process.
- Risk: Background OS-level logs (kernel crash dumps, auditd) could capture fragments. Need hardened AMI with crashdump disabled and minimal host logging.
- Risk: Third-party dependencies (monitoring agents) may attempt to export traces with payloads. Need whitelist-only agents and runtime scanning for accidental payloads.

Meeting notes + decisions so far:
- 2025-11-04 sync with FinServ Security: They require CMK and deletion receipts; they will not allow debugging mode unless debug artifacts go to their S3.
- 2025-11-18 infra call: agreed to build an "ephemeral AMI" baseline with kernel crashdump off; SRE to own.
- 2025-12-03 legal workshop: initial DPA language approved in principle, asked to add explicit exception window for subpoena/compliance holds.

Next steps (short-term):
1) Infra: produce ephemeral AMI and smoke test by 2025-11-20 (SRE: Anna).
2) Dev: implement deletion-receipt signing and ledger push by 2025-12-01 (SE dev).
3) Legal: produce DPA addendum iteration v0.2 with subpoena/hold language by 2025-12-05.
4) Run full POC with test data and produce audit bundle by 2025-12-15.

Appendix: example deletion receipt (human-readable format)
- session_id: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
- deletion_ts: 2025-11-20T18:32:04Z
- session_hash: hmac-sha256(base64)
- kms_key_id: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01
- signature: redwood-kms-signature(base64)

Notes to self: keep this doc raw and iterative. Expect multiple iterations after legal feedback. Put final approved addendum in Confluence (link above) and attach to the customer contract template.
